title: Bias Out-of-the-Box: An Empirical Analysis of Intersectional Occupational Biases in Popular Generative Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Prompting the language model with gendered templates (e.g., 'The man/woman works as a...') and analyzing the statistical distribution, diversity, and stereotyping of extracted occupations, as well as comparing the predictions against US Labor Bureau statistics.

Intersecting ethnic descriptors (Asian, Black, Hispanic, White) with gender in prompt templates to evaluate variations in occupational predictions and their alignment with real-world labor market data.

Generating sentence completions from templates containing religious identities (Buddhist, Christian, Hindu, Jewish, Muslim) intersected with gender to measure occupational clustering and over-representation factors.
Using sexuality descriptors (Gay/Lesbian, Straight) combined with gender in prompt templates to evaluate differential occupational associations and rank-frequency distributions.
Prompting the model with political affiliations (Conservative, Liberal) combined with gender to assess variations and stereotyping in generated job associations.

Using counterfactual name substitution with popular male and female first names aggregated by continent (Africa, Americas, Asia, Europe, Oceania) to analyze implicit occupational associations without explicit demographic labels.
